arxiv-2011-09205.title: Efficient Analysis of Test-beam Data with the Corryvreckan Framework
arxiv-2011-09205.creator: Jens Kröger 1,2 and Lennart Huth 3 on behalf of the CLICdp collaboration and the Corryvreckan developers
arxiv-2011-09205.description: Abstract Stringent requirements are posed on the next generations of vertex and tracking detectors for high-energy physics experiments to reach the foreseen physics goals. A large variety of silicon pixel sensors targeting the specific needs of each use case are developed and tested both in laboratory and test-beam measurement campaigns.

arxiv-2301-11994.title: Gender and Prestige Bias in Coronavirus News Reporting
arxiv-2301-11994.creator: Rebecca Dorn, Yiwen Ma, Fred Morstatter, Kristina Lerman
arxiv-2301-11994.description: Abstract . Journalists play a vital role in surfacing issues of societal importance, but their choices of what to highlight and who to interview are influenced by societal biases. In this work, we use natural language processing tools to measure these biases in a large corpus of news articles about the Covid-19 pandemic.

arxiv-2401-09798.title: All in How You Ask for It: Simple Black-Box Method for Jailbreak Attacks
arxiv-2401-09798.creator: Kazuhiro Takemoto
arxiv-2401-09798.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, encounter ‘jailbreak’ challenges, wherein safeguards are circumvented to generate ethically harmful prompts. This study introduces a straightforward black-box method for efficiently crafting jailbreak prompts, addressing the significant complexity and computational costs associated with conventional methods.

arxiv-2405-15045.title: Impact of Turbulent Magnetic Fields on Disk Formation and Fragmentation in First Star Formation
arxiv-2405-15045.creator: Kenji Eric Sadanari, Kazuyuki Omukai, Kazuyuki Sugimura, Tomoaki Matsumoto, Kengo Tomida
arxiv-2405-15045.description: Abstract Recent cosmological hydrodynamic simulations have suggested that the first stars in the universe often form as binary or multiple systems. However, previous studies typically overlooked the potential influence of magnetic fields during this process, assuming them to be weak and minimally impactful.

arxiv-2405-16633.title: Random walks on edge colored random graphs
arxiv-2405-16633.creator: Colin Cooper, Alan Frieze
arxiv-2405-16633.description: Abstract We consider random walks on edge coloured random graphs, where the colour of an edge reflects the cost of using it. In the simplest instance, the edges are coloured red or blue. Blue edges are free to use, whereas red edges incur a unit cost every time they are traversed.

arxiv-2408-14865.title: Data downlink prioritization using image classification on-board a 6U CubeSat
arxiv-2408-14865.creator: Keenan A. A. Chatar, Ezra Fielding, Kei Sano, Kentaro Kitamura
arxiv-2408-14865.description: Abstract Nanosatellites are proliferating as low-cost dedicated sensing systems with lean development cycles. Kyushu Institute of Technology (Kyutech) and collaborators have launched a joint venture for a nanosatellite mission, Visible Extra-galactic background RadiaTion Exploration by CubeSat (VERTECS). The primary mission is to elucidate the formation history of stars by observing the optical-wavelength cosmic background radiation.

arxiv-2503-01906.title: Learning to Chain Operations by Routing Information Through a Global Workspace
arxiv-2503-01906.creator: Hugo Chateau-Laurent (hugo.chateaulaurent@gmail.com), Rufin VanRullen (rufin.vanrullen@cnrs.fr)
arxiv-2503-01906.description: Abstract Abstract We present a model inspired by the Global Workspace Theory that integrates specialized modules to perform a sequential reasoning task. A controller selectively routes information between modules through the workspace using a gating mechanism. This approach allows the model to chain operations by iteratively broadcasting information between specialized domains, mimicking System-2 reasoning.

arxiv-2503-09304.title: Priority-Aware Preemptive Scheduling for Mixed-Priority Workloads in MoE Inference DOI: 10.1145/3721146.3721956 Conference: 5th Workshop on Machine Learning and Systems; March 30-April 3, 2025; Rotterdam, Netherlands ISBN: 979-8-4007-1538-9/25/03 CCS: Software and its engineering Software performanc
arxiv-2503-09304.creator: Mohammad Siavashi, Faezeh Keshmiri Dindarloo, Dejan Kostić, Marco Chiesa
arxiv-2503-09304.description: Abstract . Large Language Models have revolutionized natural language processing, yet serving them efficiently in data centers remains challenging due to mixed workloads comprising latency-sensitive (LS) and best-effort (BE) jobs. Existing inference systems employ iteration-level first-come-first-served scheduling, causing head-of-line blocking when BE jobs delay LS jobs.

arxiv-2506-02560.title: DCI: Dual-Conditional Inversion for Boosting Diffusion-Based Image Editing
arxiv-2506-02560.creator: Zixiang Li, Haoyu Wang, Wei Wang, Chuangchuang Tan, Yunchao Wei, Yao Zhao
arxiv-2506-02560.description: Abstract Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in image generation and editing tasks. Inversion within these models aims to recover the latent noise representation for a real or generated image, enabling reconstruction, editing, and other downstream tasks. However, to date, most inversion approaches suffer from an intrinsic trade-off between reconstruction accuracy and editing flexibility.

arxiv-2506-10615.title: Strongly correlated topological surface states in type-II Dirac semimetal NiTe 2
arxiv-2506-10615.creator: Neeraj Bhatt, Asif Ali, Deepali Sharma, Sakshi Bansal, Manasi Mandal, Ravi Prakash Singh, Ravi Shankar Singh
arxiv-2506-10615.description: Abstract Nontrivial topology in type-II Dirac semimetal NiTe 2 leading to topologically protected surface states give rise to fascinating phenomena holding great promise for next-generation electronic and spintronic devices. Key parameters − - such as lattice parameter, disorder, vacancies, and electron correlation − - significantly influence the electronic structure and, subsequently, the physical properties.

arxiv-2510-17967.title: Scalar fields around black hole binaries in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
arxiv-2510-17967.creator: Soumen Roy, Rodrigo Vicente, Josu C. Aurrekoetxea, Katy Clough, Pedro G. Ferreira
arxiv-2510-17967.description: Abstract Light scalar particles arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model and are well-motivated dark matter candidates. Gravitational interactions near black holes can trigger the growth of dense scalar configurations that, if sustained during inspiral, alter binary dynamics and imprint signatures on gravitational-wave signals. Detecting such effects would provide a novel probe of fundamental physics and dark matter.

europmc-pmc2622763.description: Background Reaction time (RT) is one of the most widely used measures of performance in experimental psychology, yet relatively few fMRI studies have included trial-by-trial differences in RT as a predictor variable in their analyses. Using a multi-study approach, we investigate

pmc-11395761.title: Demographic trends and disparities in mortality related to coexisting heart failure and diabetes mellitus among older adults in the United States between 1999 and 2020: A retrospective population-based cohort study from the CDC WONDER database
pmc-11395761.creator: Humza Saeed, M.B.B.S. Abdullah, Irum Naeem, Amna Zafar, Bilal Ahmad, Taimur ul Islam, Syed Saaid Rizvi, Nikita Kumari, Syed Ghazi Ali Kirmani, Fatima Mansoor, Amir Hassan, Adarsh Raja, Mohamed Daoud, Aman Goyal
pmc-11395761.description: BackgroundHeart Failure (HF) and Diabetes Mellitus (DM) often coexist, and each condition independently increases the likelihood of developing the other. While there has been concern regarding the increasing burden of disease for both conditions individually over the last decade, a comprehensive examination of mortality trends and demographic and regional disparities needs to be thoroughly explored in the United States (US).

pmc-12431776.title: The general version of Hamilton’s rule
pmc-12431776.creator: Matthijs van Veelen, Paul B Rainey, Matthijs van Veelen
pmc-12431776.description: The generality of Hamilton’s rule is much debated. In this paper, I show that this debate can be resolved by constructing a general version of Hamilton’s rule, which allows for a large variety of ways in which the fitness of an individual can depend on the social behavior of oneself and of others.

pmc-12706649.title: Nutritional and Phytochemical Potential of Two Local Food Plants in Burkina Faso: Crateva adansonii and Capparis corymbosa
pmc-12706649.creator: Edwige Noëlle Roamba, Frédéric Anderson Konkobo, Poussian Raymond Barry, Adama Pamba Séré, Abdoudramane Sanou, Roger Dakuyo, Kabakdé Kaboré, Kiessoun Konaté, Mamoudou Hama Dicko
pmc-12706649.description: This study focused on the biochemical and nutritional characterization of two edible plant species in Burkina Faso: Capparis corymbosa and Crateva adansonii. The objective was to evaluate their proximate composition, their content of primary and secondary metabolites, minerals, and amino acids, as well as their antioxidant potential, with a view to enhancing their nutritional value.

pmc-12733393.title: Porcine Corneal Models as Translational Platforms for Innovative Therapies: Current Insights and Future Directions
pmc-12733393.creator: Patrícia Nápoles, Mónica Faria, Elisa Julião Campos, Dimitrios Karamichos
pmc-12733393.description: The development of advanced biomaterials for corneal applications requires robust translational platforms that faithfully replicate human characteristics. Porcine corneas are increasingly recognized for ophthalmic research. Their unique combination of anatomical similarity, biomechanical comparability, and accessibility make them highly suitable for preclinical evaluation of innovative therapies, bridging the gap between preclinical discovery and clinical application.

pmc-12829184.title: Unexpected migration patterns in a high-latitude breeding songbird: evidence from multi-sensor geolocators and isotopes
pmc-12829184.creator: Stephanie J. Szarmach, Johanna K. Beam, Mads Moore, Benjamin M. Van Doren, Alan Brelsford, David P. L. Toews
pmc-12829184.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMigratory birds often exhibit within-species variation in migration routes and non-breeding areas, yet the mechanisms shaping these patterns remain poorly understood, particularly in high-latitude breeding populations. Several hypotheses have been proposed to explain why birds follow particular routes: optimal migration theory proposes that routes minimizing time or energy expenditure are favored, whereas the historical contingency hypothesis posits that routes are shaped by past range expansion, sometimes resulting in “suboptimal” migrations.

pmc-13053650.title: Thymoquinone Enhances Tamoxifen Efficacy Against Triple‐Negative Breast Cancer by Targeting EMT Signaling
pmc-13053650.creator: Mazharul Haque, Ritis K. Shyanti, Sudhanshu Sharma, Hongzhuan Wu, Manoj K. Mishra
pmc-13053650.description: The variety of available therapies for treating TNBC is constrained by the minimal or no expression of receptors such as estrogen (ER), progesterone (PR), and human epidermal growth factor 2 (HER2). However, estrogen receptor β (ERβ) has emerged as a potential therapeutic target for TNBCs.

pmc-13485701.title: Status quo bias drives public support for drug policy in the USA
pmc-13485701.creator: Bence Hamrak, Gabor Simonovits
pmc-13485701.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Substance regulation in the USA is in a crisis. Here we explore whether seemingly misaligned policies contradict public preferences or reflect biased citizen opinions. Using survey data (N = 5,053), we show that policy outcomes align with public opinion.

pmc-7618755.title: Rigid, bivalent CTLA-4 binding to CD80 is required to disrupt the cis CD80/PD-L1 interaction
pmc-7618755.creator: Maximillian A. Robinson, Alan Kennedy, Carolina T. Orozco, Hung-Chang Chen, Erin Waters, Dalisay Giovacchini, Kay Yeung, Lily Filer, Claudia Hinze, Christopher Lloyd, Simon J. Dovedi, and David M. Sansom
pmc-7618755.description: SummaryThe CTLA-4 and PD-1 checkpoints control immune responses and are key targets in immunotherapy. Both pathways are connected via a cis interaction between CD80 and PD-L1, the ligands for CTLA-4 and PD-1, respectively. This cis interaction prevents PD-1-PD-L1 binding but is reversed by CTLA-4 trans-endocytosis of CD80. However, how CTLA-4 selectively removes CD80, but not PD-L1, is unclear.

uslaw-usc-t22-s2520.title: 22 U.S.C. § 2520 — Military training and service exemption
uslaw-usc-t22-s2520.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s2520.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 34 (The Peace Corps). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding the provisions of any other law or regulation, service in the Peace Corps as a volunteer shall not in any way exempt such volunteer from the performance of any obligations or duties under the provisions of the Universal Military Training and Service.
